chunks.text: Elizabeth Bennet walked three miles through the mud to Netherfield Park to see her sister Jane, who had caught a chill.
Despite his early harsh judgment of her looks, Mr. Darcy found himself admiring the fine expression of Elizabeth's dark eyes.
Mr. Bingley took the lease on Netherfield Park and soon hosted a ball for the entire neighbourhood.
Mr. Collins, a pompous clergyman, proposed marriage to Elizabeth Bennet, and she refused him without hesitation.
Charlotte Lucas accepted Mr. Collins's proposal within days, valuing a comfortable home over any romantic attachment.
Mr. Wickham told Elizabeth a convincing but false story, blaming Mr. Darcy for ruining his prospects in life.
Lydia Bennet ran off with Mr. Wickham to London, throwing the whole family into a scandal.
Unknown to the Bennets, Mr. Darcy quietly paid off Wickham's debts to save the family's reputation.
Lady Catherine de Bourgh arrived unannounced to demand that Elizabeth promise never to marry her nephew.
In his letter, Mr. Darcy explained his part in persuading Mr. Bingley to leave Jane and Netherfield.
Jane Bennet fell ill with a bad cold after riding to Netherfield in the pouring rain on her mother's insistence.
Mr. Bennet found endless amusement in teasing his wife about her obsession with marrying off their five daughters.
Mrs. Bennet was overjoyed the moment she saw how attentive Mr. Bingley had become toward her daughter Jane.
While touring Derbyshire with her aunt and uncle, Elizabeth was persuaded to visit Pemberley, Mr. Darcy's grand estate.
After the scandal had passed, Mr. Darcy proposed to Elizabeth a second time, and this time she gladly accepted.
Miss Caroline Bingley made repeated, thinly veiled attempts to turn Mr. Darcy's attention away from Elizabeth.
The Bennet family estate was entailed away from the five daughters, destined instead for their distant cousin Mr. Collins.
Elizabeth and Jane spoke quietly together about their youngest sister Lydia's reckless flirting with the militia officers.
Colonel Fitzwilliam let slip to Elizabeth that his cousin Mr. Darcy had been responsible for separating Bingley from Jane.
At the Netherfield ball, the whole Bennet family attended, and Mr. Darcy surprised everyone by asking Elizabeth to dance.
